documents.title: AI Policy for Faculty and Students
documents.stance_why: The policy sets no rule itself: it says "instructors have broad discretion to determine the appropriate use of AI tools" and "The right to use and the extent of AI tool use for a particular course is at the faculty's discretion", so the decision is delegated.
documents.summary: The Provost's university-wide AI policy welcomes responsible AI use but gives instructors broad discretion, asks them to state an AI policy in the syllabus, and makes students answerable for final work and for evaluating AI output. It also cautions faculty against relying on AI detectors alone and lists other evidence of misuse.

units.why: The opening sentence states the university's position: it "recognizes the significant contributions and pedagogical value" of AI alongside "challenges and pitfalls". This is an institution-level framing principle, so P56 (framework/preamble) and not a rule on use.
units.anchor: recognizes the significant contributions and pedagogical value that Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools offer

units.why: States that AI technologies are "integral to academic and professional disciplines", a rationale tying AI to professional relevance, so P44 (AI as a professional skill) fits better than the generic framework type P56.
units.anchor: integral to academic and professional disciplines and enhance courses and curricula

units.why: "Faculty and students are encouraged to use AI responsibly" sets a default welcoming stance for everyone, so P02 (permit or encourage by default), actor all, modality should.
units.anchor: Faculty and students are encouraged to use AI responsibly

units.why: The requirements of "transparency, fairness, and respect for privacy" are principles for AI use at the institution level; P56 (principles) rather than P50 because privacy is only one of three named principles with no operative rule.
units.anchor: ensuring transparency, fairness, and respect for privacy

units.why: Says "appropriate ethical use will change over time", an acknowledgement that the policy and norms will evolve, which is P54 (revisit regularly).
units.anchor: recognition that appropriate ethical use will change over time

units.why: "instructors have broad discretion to determine the appropriate use of AI tools" hands the decision to instructors; P04 (let each instructor set the rule) is the exact fit, and it is the basis for the delegates stance.
units.anchor: instructors have broad discretion to determine the appropriate use of AI tools in their classrooms

units.why: "the extent of AI tool use for a particular course is at the faculty's discretion" with "specific conditions and criteria for permitted applications" is again per-instructor control (P04); it adds that instructors may set conditions on permitted uses.
units.anchor: the extent of AI tool use for a particular course is at the faculty's discretion

units.why: "The instructor should provide a clear statement about AI utilization in their course syllabus" requires a syllabus AI statement; P09 matches directly.
units.anchor: The instructor should provide a clear statement about AI utilization in their course syllabus

units.why: Instructors should "respond to any student inquiries on the subject"; this is the instructor-side counterpart of students asking before using AI. P10 is the nearest type (asking and answering questions about permission); no type covers instructor responsiveness more precisely.
units.anchor: respond to any student inquiries on the subject

units.why: "strongly recommended that the instructor discuss the statement at the course's beginning and as necessary throughout" is about communicating the AI expectations repeatedly; P09 (state expectations) is the closest communicate-theme type.
units.anchor: strongly recommended that the instructor discuss the statement at the course's beginning

units.why: "Students must read and abide by any statements in the syllabus regarding AI" binds students to whatever the instructor sets, which is P04 (rule set per instructor) from the student side; P10 does not fit because it is not about asking.
units.anchor: Students must read and abide by any statements in the syllabus regarding AI

units.why: Students should "seek further information from any instructor if needed" when unsure about AI rules, directly P10.
units.anchor: seek further information from any instructor if needed

units.why: "Please note citation requirements in each course syllabus" tells students to follow the course's citation rule for AI content; P24 (disclose/cite) and not P04 because the subject is citation.
units.anchor: Please note citation requirements in each course syllabus

units.why: A fallback: "If the instructor does not provide guidance, students should cite content derived from AI tools". It concerns citation so I chose P24; P06 covers silence on whether AI is allowed, which this does not address.
units.anchor: students should cite content derived from AI tools using the style most closely resembling
units.frag_start: If the instructor does not provide

units.why: "All final works are the sole responsibility of the student" makes students answerable for what they submit: P29.
units.anchor: All final works are the sole responsibility of the student

units.why: "AI tools can generate false or biased content" is a factual warning that output is unreliable: P31 (output may be wrong).
units.anchor: AI tools can generate false or biased content

units.why: "essential for students to critically evaluate AI generated content before including it in submitted assignments" is a duty to verify output: P31.
units.anchor: essential for students to critically evaluate AI generated content before including it in submitted assignments

units.why: Encourages use of Library "databases and research tools ... approved for use in coursework"; pointing students to institutionally approved tools matches P50 (prefer vetted tools), not P17 since no AI tool is provided.
units.anchor: encouraged to utilize all databases and research tools provided by the
units.frag_start: Faculty and students are encouraged to utilize
units.frag_end: unless specified otherwise by an instructor

units.why: "should not rely on AI detection as the sole source of evidence" limits use of detectors due to "inconsistent accuracy": P39.
units.anchor: faculty should not rely on AI detection as the sole source of evidence

units.why: "instructors should consider multiple forms of evidence when evaluating potential misuses" tells faculty to gather evidence beyond detectors: P40 (process evidence).
units.anchor: instructors should consider multiple forms of evidence when evaluating potential misuses of AI

units.why: The bulleted list names signs of misuse such as "Inconsistencies in writing style or quality compared to previous assignments"; these are evidence indicators, so P40.
units.anchor: Inconsistencies in writing style or quality compared to previous assignments

units.why: "the procedure for handling violations of the honor code" points suspected AI misuse into the Honor Code process, matching P36 (misconduct handled by integrity processes).
units.anchor: View the procedure for handling violations of the honor code here

documents.title: Resources for Generative AI in Teaching and Learning
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university-wide permission or ban; it says "the use of generative artificial intelligence tools must be consistent with the instructor’s stated course policy" and otherwise offers advice, so it delegates.
documents.summary: A faculty resource page that defines generative AI, tells instructors to communicate expectations clearly and says student AI use must follow the instructor's course policy. It mostly offers assessment-design tips and points to workshops and readings.

units.why: Defines generative AI as "tools such as ChatGPT or Dall-E 2 that can create sophisticated novel text, images", setting what the page covers: P61.
units.anchor: artificial intelligence or machine learning tools such as ChatGPT or Dall-E 2

units.why: Notes that generated "responses often include inaccuracies", a fact about unreliable output that supports verifying it: P31.
units.anchor: responses often include inaccuracies

units.why: "Your expectations should be clearly communicated with your students" tells instructors to state AI expectations: P09.
units.anchor: Your expectations should be clearly communicated with your students

units.why: "the use of generative artificial intelligence tools must be consistent with the instructor's stated course policy" binds students to instructor-set rules: P04.
units.anchor: must be consistent with the instructor’s stated course policy

units.why: Observes that paid services and paraphrasers create "additional challenges for text-based detection"; this is a statement about limits of detection, P39.
units.anchor: creating additional challenges for text-based detection

units.why: Says the ability to discern machine text "will diminish and will therefore require a different approach", an argument against relying on detection: P39.
units.anchor: the ability to discern machine-generated text from human-generated text will diminish

units.why: "Start with learning objectives (backwards design)" advises designing assessment from objectives in response to AI; P35.
units.anchor: Start with learning objectives (backwards design)

units.why: "Design assignments that provide opportunities for students to get feedback ... and apply it" is an assignment redesign tip: P35.
units.anchor: Design assignments that provide opportunities for students to get feedback from you or peers

units.why: "Develop a rubric and make it available to students with the assessment" is a grading-design tip within AI-response assessment design: P35.
units.anchor: Develop a rubric and make it available to students with the assessment

units.why: "Ask students to write a paper that incorporates aspects from the live class discussion" redesigns the task so generic AI output is less useful: P35.
units.anchor: Ask students to write a paper that incorporates aspects from the live class discussion

units.why: "reflect and share their process by either giving a presentation ... Build in time to allow both you and other students to ask questions" checks understanding by questioning, so P34 rather than P35.
units.anchor: Ask students to reflect and share their process by either giving a presentation

units.why: "Require students to submit written assignments using Google Docs" so revision history makes the process transparent; this is process evidence (P40), not a redesign (P35).
units.anchor: Require students to submit written assignments using Google Docs

units.why: Faculty suggestion: "Asking students to document their process for an assignment ... and citing sources" asks students to record process, P26.
units.anchor: Asking students to document their process for an assignment

units.why: "Giving students options to submit learning artifacts in various formats such as audio files, multimedia projects" is an assignment redesign suggestion: P35.
units.anchor: Giving students options to submit learning artifacts in various formats

units.why: "Reflecting on real-life experiences, students can describe their feelings" proposes personal-experience assignments that are harder to outsource: P35.
units.anchor: Reflecting on real-life experiences, students can describe their feelings

units.why: "Commenting on thoughts and discussing any misconceptions they may have in a peer discussion" is a peer-discussion assessment suggestion: P35.
units.anchor: Commenting on thoughts and discussing any misconceptions they may have in a peer discussion

units.why: "Ask students to generate an outline and then critique it" turns a task into critical evaluation; chosen P35 because it is an assignment design, not a rule on verifying AI output.
units.anchor: Ask students to generate an outline and then critique it

units.why: "Submit a program or line of code then ask students to evaluate the response" is a coding-specific assignment redesign that has students evaluate given output: P35.
units.anchor: Submit a program or line of code then ask students to evaluate the response

units.why: "A bigger assignment is broken down into smaller pieces so students can submit along the way and receive feedback" is staged-submission redesign: P35.
units.anchor: A bigger assignment is broken down into smaller pieces

units.why: Describes an online workshop on "teaching approaches and digital tools you can use to promote academic honesty", a faculty support resource: P63.
units.anchor: the teaching approaches and digital tools you can use to promote academic honesty

units.why: "Have a suggestion or tip to add?" with a Submit a Teaching Tip button invites feedback on the resource, close to P54 (feedback invited); this is the only type about soliciting input.
units.anchor: Have a suggestion or tip to add?

documents.title: Syllabus wording: AI prohibited
documents.stance_why: The wording says "You may not use AI or ML tools ... on assignments, discussions, exams, and presentations in this course", a ban on all course work.
documents.summary: A university-provided syllabus statement that instructors can adopt to ban all AI/ML tools on assignments, discussions, exams and presentations. It frames use as unauthorized assistance and an Honor Code violation, with general academic-integrity boilerplate.

units.why: "You may not use AI or ML tools ... on assignments, discussions, exams, and presentations in this course" is a blanket ban on all graded work: P01 (it also covers exams, but the ban is one rule so one unit).
units.anchor: You may not use AI or ML tools, such as ChatGPT or Dall-E

units.why: "expected to complete each assignment without assistance from others, including AI/ML automated tools" requires work to be unassisted by AI; P19 fits, since the focus is on work being done by the student.
units.anchor: complete each assignment without assistance from others, including AI/ML automated tools

units.why: "constitutes the receiving of unauthorized assistance for academic work and is a violation of the Hofstra University Honor Code" classes AI use as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: is a violation of the Hofstra University Honor Code

units.why: The boilerplate says work is "done, entirely and without unauthorized assistance, by the individual(s) whose name(s) it bears", a rule that submitted work be the student's own: P29.
units.anchor: is done, entirely and without unauthorized assistance, by the individual(s) whose name(s) it bears

units.why: "will not offer the privileges of the community to the repeat offender" states escalated consequences by offense, a penalty stated in advance: P37.
units.anchor: it will not offer the privileges of the community to the repeat offender

units.why: "Students bear the ultimate responsibility for implementing the principles of academic integrity" places responsibility on students: P29.
units.anchor: Students bear the ultimate responsibility for implementing the principles of academic integrity

documents.title: Syllabus wording: AI use with acknowledgement
documents.stance_why: The wording says "You may use AI/ML tools such as ChatGPT or Dall-E on assignments, discussions, exams, and presentations in this course if you use clear and accurate citations", i.e. allowed with a disclosure condition.
documents.summary: A university-provided syllabus statement permitting AI/ML tools on all course work, including exams, provided each use is cited in the submission. It repeats the standard academic-integrity paragraph.

units.why: "You may use AI/ML tools such as ChatGPT or Dall-E on assignments, discussions, exams, and presentations" is a default permission, including exams, subject to citation: P02.
units.anchor: You may use AI/ML tools such as ChatGPT or Dall-E on assignments, discussions, exams

units.why: The condition "citations in the assignment submission where and how AI/ML tools have been used" requires marking the place and manner of use in the submission; chosen P27 over P24 for the "where and how" wording.
units.anchor: citations in the assignment submission where and how AI/ML tools have been used
units.frag_start: if you use clear and accurate

units.why: "Any assignment that was completed with AI/ML tools must contain an appropriate citation" is a plain citation requirement for each submission: P24.
units.anchor: Any assignment that was completed with AI/ML tools must contain an appropriate citation

units.why: The boilerplate says work is "done, entirely and without unauthorized assistance, by the individual(s) whose name(s) it bears", a rule that submitted work be the student's own: P29.
units.anchor: is done, entirely and without unauthorized assistance, by the individual(s) whose name(s) it bears

units.why: "will not offer the privileges of the community to the repeat offender" states escalated consequences by offense, a penalty stated in advance: P37.
units.anchor: it will not offer the privileges of the community to the repeat offender

units.why: "Students bear the ultimate responsibility for implementing the principles of academic integrity" places responsibility on students: P29.
units.anchor: Students bear the ultimate responsibility for implementing the principles of academic integrity
